profile.name: right and left grand
profile.tagline: A classic square dance move where eight dancers weave through alternating hand pull-bys.
profile.insight: In right and left grand, men circle counter-clockwise and women clockwise, passing four partners with alternating right and left hand pull-bys.
profile.profile: Right and left grand is a foundational square dance move involving eight dancers arranged in a square or circle. Each dancer alternates passing by others using right and left hand pull-bys, moving men counter-clockwise and women clockwise. The move takes about 10 counts and ends with dancers halfway across the set, facing their original partner or the person they started with. Variants include weave the ring and wrong way grand, distinguished by hand contact and direction of movement.
profile.profile_long: Right and left grand, also called grand right and left, is a fundamental move in modern Western square dancing, performed by eight dancers arranged typically in a square set. At the start, dancers face their partner or adjust their orientation by turning up to 90 degrees to do so. The move consists of four alternating hand pull-bys: right hand pull by, left hand pull by, right hand pull by, and left hand pull by. Each pull by involves stepping forward with hands held and releasing the hand hold as dancers pass right or left shoulders. Men travel counter-clockwise around the ring, while women travel clockwise, creating a weaving pattern through the set. The move takes approximately 10 counts to complete, ending with dancers halfway across the set, facing the same person they began with, who may or may not be their original partner. Styling flourishes may be added but the basic pattern remains consistent. The right and left grand family includes related calls such as weave the ring, which is performed without hand contact, and wrong way grand, where dancers face away from their partner and reverse the direction of travel. This move is one of the most recognizable calls in square dancing, alongside the promenade and dosado. It can be performed in a square or large circle formation and is a staple in the repertoire of square dance callers worldwide.

sections.origins_and_history: Right and left grand is a classic square dance move widely used in modern Western square dancing. It is known in English country dance as the Grand Chain and has been adapted into various forms within square dance traditions. The move is part of the standard repertoire taught and called by square dance callers internationally.
sections.how_it_is_danced: Dancers begin facing their partner, adjusting orientation if necessary. Each dancer extends the right hand to the person faced and performs a right-hand pull by, stepping forward and passing right shoulders. Next, they extend the left hand to the next person and perform a left-hand pull by, passing left shoulders. This sequence repeats twice more, alternating right and left hands, with men moving counter-clockwise and women clockwise around the set. The move completes in about 10 counts. Styling flourishes may be added but are not required.
sections.costume_and_setting: Performed in a square or large circle formation, typically at square dance events or clubs. No specific costume details are provided in the sources.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: Right and left grand is a common call in square dance events, used to engage all dancers in a flowing, communal movement. It is a social dance move rather than a ritual or sacred dance.
sections.regional_variants: The move is known as Grand Chain in English country dances and has variants within the right and left grand family, including weave the ring (no hand contact) and wrong way grand (facing away from partner and reversing direction).
sections.lineage: Derived from traditional English country dance moves, adapted into modern Western square dance. It is part of the core vocabulary of square dance calls standardized by organizations such as Callerlab.
